target_customer: Game developers at founding; now developers building agent and realtime backends
problem: Hosting multiplayer game servers needs matchmaking, scaling and DDoS protection that small studios struggle to build; later, agent workloads need durable stateful runtimes.
business_model: Open-source (Apache 2.0) with managed cloud usage pricing (pricing not found)
product_category: Game server orchestration, now actor-based orchestrator for agents

founders.name: Nicholas Kissel
previous_startups: Small game studio with Nathan Flurry

founders.name: Nathaniel Flurry
previous_startups: Small game studio with four launched games
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built Krunker.io infrastructure in high school and was an Apple WWDC scholar 2016 to 2018. Education beyond high school is not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a scalable game server orchestrator with matchmaking and DDoS mitigation, later a Durable Objects style runtime, requires distributed systems work.

defensibility.rationale: Open source under Apache 2.0 limits lock-in; infrastructure integration gives modest switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Multiplay was shut down on March 31, 2026 and Hathora closed on May 5, 2026 after an acquisition, per undated vendor blogs; Rivet pivoted to agent infrastructure.

market_need_then: The YC launch framed it as Heroku for multiplayer games, but no demand or spend data was opened.

branding.domain_note: Started on rivet.gg and moved to rivet.dev; both still used. Acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Black and white logo versions with a public brand page and product marks for Actors, Workflows and Cloud
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, with 'The actor guy' as a founder bio flourish

rebrands.why: Positioning change; the name stayed the same and no announcement was found.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source on GitHub, Godot asset library listing and a Show HN post for Rivet Actors; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Common word shared with unrelated companies, but kept through a positioning change; modest open-source community.

pivots.from: Heroku for multiplayer games (managed game servers, matchmaking, DDoS mitigation)
pivots.to: Open-source orchestrator for agentic workloads and Durable Objects alternative
pivots.why: Not stated by the company; date not found.

outcome_analysis: Rivet began as a managed game server platform in YC W23 and repositioned to an open-source actor orchestrator for agents, now backed by YC and a16z Speedrun with a team of seven. The game backend market saw shutdowns of Multiplay and Hathora in 2026, which may support the pivot, though the founders have not said why they moved. Funding beyond the YC deal is not public, so traction is unclear.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights lists a $500K convertible note from Y Combinator dated January 2023, which is the standard YC deal and is not recorded as a round; an a16z Speedrun backing is stated on the company site without amount or date. Seedtable shows $500K on 2023-02-27. Another CB Insights line of $0.25M from a Morgan Stanley fund in September 2025 could not be tied to this company. Other companies named Rivet (dating app, Ethereum infrastructure) were excluded. The YC page founded year is 2023 while aggregators say 2022; 2022 used from a directory and unverified. The success factor successful_pivot is a judgment, not backed by revenue data. No competitor source dated near the batch was found, so the list is empty; the named incumbents come from undated 2026 vendor pages. Completeness pass: the 500K convertible note rests on CB Insights (Seedtable dates a 500K round 2023-02-27; one aggregator also lists a 130K seed from YC that was not recorded because its source is unclear). The CB Insights page could not be opened for confirmation, so the entity match is unverified. No a16z amount found.
